raw_response:
I farm the same 6 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will put all 6 mu into wheat in the winter season and all 6 mu into maize after wheat comes off. I do not like making big changes unless I see it work nearby, and around here if fertilizer is too short, yield drops fast and that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I have well water, so I will use irrigation to hold the crop steady when the weather is dry. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed, use more base fertilizer, then add nitrogen again at greening or jointing. Wheat needs steady feeding and water, otherwise the heads do not fill well. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives better yield here if fertilizer and water keep up. I will put fertilizer mainly before sowing and then topdress nitrogen around the big bell mouth stage. I have only 2 people at home and some off-farm work, so I will keep the tillage simple with rotary tillage, not too many field passes. I will still spray when needed because if rust, aphids, armyworm, or corn borer get ahead of me, I lose grain fast. This year I will aim for a solid harvest, not the cheapest plan and not a risky plan.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will keep my 6 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that is what fits my land, water, and labor. I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because losing yield costs more than using a bit extra. For wheat I will use improved seed, steady fertilizer, and three irrigations to hold tillers and grain filling. For maize I will use hybrid seed, enough nitrogen, and two irrigations so the ears can fill well in summer.
